Finding Leaks

How to Locate Underground Water Lines on Your Property

By SRQ Leak Pros Editorial · Published November 5, 2026 · Updated November 7, 2026 · 7 min read

Short answer: To locate underground water lines, start at the water meter and the spot where the pipe enters your house, then trace the path between them. Records, a metal detector or a pipe locator can help on metal pipe. Plastic lines often need a trace wire or a pro's tools. Call Sunshine 811 first so utility lines get marked.

Knowing how to locate underground water lines saves you from a broken pipe and a flooded yard. It also speeds up any leak repair, because the crew doesn't have to guess. If you're chasing a hidden leak, SRQ Leak Pros can connect you with a local provider for underground leak detection in Sarasota.

This guide walks through what you can do yourself and when the job needs a locator.

Why it matters where your water line runs

A buried service line is easy to hit and hard to see. Fence posts, tree planting, irrigation work and pool projects all put it at risk. If a leak shows up, knowing the path also narrows the search area. That can mean one small hole instead of a long trench.

How to locate underground water lines yourself

Use these steps in order. Stop if you're unsure.

  1. Find the meter box. It usually sits near the street or sidewalk, under a small lid. The pipe on the house side of the meter is your service line.
  2. Find the house entry. Look for the main shut-off valve or the pipe rising out of the ground near a hose bib, garage or utility room.
  3. Draw a straight line. Most service lines run fairly straight between those two points, though not always.
  4. Check records. Look for a plat, survey, permit drawings or a repair invoice. Some show the line's route.
  5. Look for clues. Sunken strips of lawn, a line of greener grass or patched concrete can trace an old trench.
  6. Try a locator on metal pipe. Copper and galvanized lines can carry a signal from a rented pipe locator.
  7. Confirm by hand. Before any heavy digging, expose the pipe at one spot with a hand tool.

Keep hand digging shallow. Under Florida Statutes § 556.108, a single-family homeowner may dig on their own land without an 811 notice only to a depth of 10 inches, with due care and outside utility easements.

What will Sunshine 811 mark?

Sunshine 811 sends your dig notice to member utilities, and each marks its own buried lines. Florida requires that call at least two full business days before you dig. The marks show public lines such as gas, power, cable and the utility's water pipe. Your private service line from the meter to the house is generally not part of those marks. Neither are sprinkler lines or pool pipes.

LineMarked through 811?How to find it
Gas, power, cable, phoneYes, by each member utilityWait for paint or flags
Utility water pipe to the meterUsually, by the utilityWait for marks
Service line, meter to houseUsually notTrace it yourself or hire a locator
Irrigation linesNoFollow zones from the valve box
Pool plumbingNoStart at the pump and filter

How do pros locate water lines?

Pros use several tools, often together:

  • Pipe and cable locator. A transmitter puts a signal on metal pipe or a trace wire. A receiver follows the signal and estimates depth.
  • Trace wire. A copper wire laid beside plastic pipe at install. If it exists and is intact, the line is easy to follow.
  • Sonde. A small transmitter pushed or pulled inside a pipe. The receiver tracks it from above.
  • Ground microphone. On a leaking line, the hiss of escaping water reveals the path and the leak point.
  • Ground-penetrating radar (GPR). Radar pulses can show buried objects, including some plastic pipes, in the right soil.
  • Vacuum excavation. A pro exposes the pipe with air or water and a vacuum, without a sharp shovel.

Wikipedia's leak detection article lists acoustic and other methods used to find leaks in buried pipes. The same tools help trace the pipe itself.

How to find a plastic water line

Plastic is the hard case. PVC, PEX and polybutylene don't carry a locator signal. Options include:

  • Look for a trace wire at the meter box or house end.
  • Push a sonde into the line, where access allows.
  • Use GPR in dry, sandy soil, where it tends to work better.
  • Run water and listen with a ground microphone if the line leaks.
  • Pot-hole at a few points along the likely path.

Can a metal detector find a water line?

Sometimes. A metal detector can find a shallow copper or galvanized line, or metal fittings on a plastic one. It won't follow a plastic line well. Depth and nearby metal, such as rebar or old fencing, can confuse it.

Do dowsing rods find water pipes?

There is no reliable evidence that dowsing rods find pipes. Use records, tracing tools or a pro instead. A wrong guess can cost far more than a locate.

Sarasota tips for finding a water line

Sarasota homes often have meter boxes near the street and long runs to the house on deep lots. Irrigation lines cross many yards and can be mistaken for the service line. Many newer homes use plastic service pipe, which needs a trace wire or a pro.

Sarasota County's leak FAQ explains that its staff check reported leaks and decide whether the problem is the county's or the customer's. If a wet spot sits near the meter, call your utility first. Florida law puts repair of the line from the meter to the building within a plumbing contractor's scope.

How to keep your line easy to find

  • Save a sketch of the route with measurements from fixed points.
  • Keep repair invoices and permits in your home file.
  • Ask for a trace wire on any new plastic line.
  • Mark the meter box and the main shut-off clearly.

What locating tools can homeowners rent?

Some rental counters and hardware stores carry basic pipe and cable locators. They work on metal pipe or on a plastic line with an intact trace wire. A rental set has two parts: a transmitter that clamps to or connects with the pipe, and a handheld receiver that beeps or shows a signal over it.

ToolWorks onLimits for a homeowner
Pipe and cable locatorCopper, galvanized, traced plasticNeeds a clean connection point
Metal detectorShallow metal pipe and fittingsConfused by rebar and debris
Probe rodShallow pipe in soft soilCan puncture thin plastic pipe
Hose and listeningA leaking lineOnly works if the line leaks

Ground-penetrating radar and sondes are usually pro tools. They take training to read well.

Common mistakes when locating a water line

  • Trusting one clue. A green strip may be an old irrigation trench, not the service line.
  • Assuming a straight path. Lines bend around trees, slabs and past repairs.
  • Probing too hard. A steel rod can pierce PEX or polybutylene.
  • Skipping 811. Gas and power lines may share the same path.
  • Digging with power tools. Augers and trenchers cut pipe before you feel it.
  • Forgetting the sprinklers. Irrigation mains often cross the service line.

If a clue doesn't line up with the meter and the house entry, stop and confirm before you dig.

Local note: deep lots in North Port often mean long service lines with few visible clues. In Bradenton, older homes may have metal lines that trace easily. On Longboat Key, tight lots put utility lines close together, so marks matter.

Related reading: once you know the route, learn how deep water lines are buried. If the line leaks, read how to find a water leak underground. For leaks near a slab or hardscape, see water leak under the driveway.

When should you call a leak detection professional?

Call a pro when:

  • You need to dig and can't confirm the route
  • The line is plastic with no trace wire
  • You see a wet spot, sinkhole or high bill with no clear cause
  • You plan a pool, fence or tree near the likely path

Frequently asked questions

Who can locate my private water line?

A leak detection company or a plumbing provider with locating gear can trace it. The utility usually marks only its own lines.

How much does it cost to locate a water line?

Prices vary with line material, length and access. Ask for a quote that lists whether locating, depth checks and leak detection are included.

Can I use my phone to find a water pipe?

Phone apps that claim to find pipes are not reliable. Use records, a locator or a pro.

How do I find my water line without a trace wire?

Start at the meter and the house entry and connect them. A pro can then use a sonde, ground-penetrating radar or acoustic listening to confirm.
